description: Manually labelled questions from inspected PDFs: LangChain component notes (sample.pdf / langchain_components.pdf) and Non-Native Prompt Engineering Risks. Labels use doc_key + page. chunk_ids are null until filled after a chunk inventory. document_id values are resolved at runtime from the registry.

documents.notes: sample.pdf is a duplicate of the same notes; prefer the langchain_components original name when both exist.

documents.match_original_filename: Non-Native Prompt Engineering Risks - Google Gemini.pdf
documents.notes: Match by original filename or stored-filename substring.

questions.question: What are the six major LangChain components?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Lists Models, Prompts, Chains, Memory, Indexes, Agents.

questions.question: Which LangChain component is explored first in the notes?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Mentions the Model component.

questions.question: What API problem do different LLM providers create?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Different providers expose different APIs/code styles and switching requires rewriting code.

questions.question: How does LangChain solve provider API differences for models?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Provides a standardized interface so only a few lines change when switching providers.

questions.question: What input/output behaviour do embedding models follow?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Text-in, vector-out.

questions.question: Name uses of embedding models listed in the notes.
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Includes semantic search, RAG, similarity matching, clustering/indexing.

questions.question: What are the two model types highlighted in the Model Component summary?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Language models and embedding models.

questions.question: What is the key takeaway of LangChain's Model Component?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: It standardizes talking to LLMs so providers can be switched without rewriting the codebase.

questions.question: What kinds of prompts does LangChain's Prompt component help design?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Dynamic, role-based, few-shot, structured prompts / templates with placeholders.

questions.question: Give an example of a dynamic prompt template from the notes.
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Mentions a template like Summarize {topic} in {tone}.

questions.question: What are few-shot prompts used for according to the notes?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Showing examples first; used in customer support, classification, pattern tasks.

questions.question: Why is the product named LangChain according to the notes?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: The name comes from the idea of Chains as pipelines of steps.

questions.question: What is a Chain in LangChain?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: A pipeline where the output of one step becomes the input of the next.

questions.question: What are sequential chains ideal for?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Examples like translate→summarize, extract→validate→format, retrieve→answer.

questions.question: How can a sentiment-based chain route user feedback?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Positive feedback gets a thank-you path; negative feedback can email support.

questions.question: Why are Indexes needed for private documents?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: LLMs are trained on public data; indexes let the model use private/internal documents.

questions.question: Why do text splitters break large documents into chunks?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Large documents cannot be embedded directly; chunks prepare text for semantic search.

questions.question: Describe the process to answer questions from a company rules PDF using indexes.
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Load PDF, split into chunks, create embeddings/vector store, then retrieve.

questions.question: Which four index-related pieces work together for semantic search?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Document loaders, text splitters, vector stores, and retrievers.

questions.question: What is the limitation of storing full conversation history in memory?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Long conversations increase token cost heavily.

questions.question: What does ConversationBufferWindowMemory store?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Only the last N interactions / a window of recent messages.

questions.question: What do LangChain Agents allow you to build?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: AI agents that can reason and use tools / act beyond plain chatbots.

questions.question: What reasoning technique is mentioned for agents?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Chain-of-Thought reasoning / step-by-step planning.

questions.question: What kinds of tools can agents access?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: External tools such as APIs, web search, and similar actions.

questions.question: Why do AI agents matter compared with chatbots?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: They can fetch live info, run workflows, multi-step tasks, interact with systems.

questions.question: Which pages discuss embedding models and providers?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Should cite pages covering embedding models and supported providers.

questions.question: Where does the notes section on Memory begin?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Mentions Memory as a LangChain component around the later pages.

questions.question: What company is used as the AI-native SaaS example in the prompt-engineering risks document?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Worktual.

questions.question: Why can a polite customer-support system prompt fall short?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Vague instructions like speak nicely / apologize a lot create a fake, overly subservient tone.

questions.question: What speech-related cues are missing when prompts lack cadence guidance?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Pauses, interruptions, or backchanneling such as Mm-hmm.

questions.question: Why is 'Speak in a friendly voice' ineffective for audio prompts?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: It is vague and does not give effective audio/voice instructions.

questions.question: What specialized tasks need rigorous system prompts according to the document?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Code review and debugging.

questions.question: What evaluation criteria are mentioned for prompt output quality?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Tone alignment, adherence to constraints, and hallucination rate.

questions.question: What is regression testing used for in prompt changes?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: Catching cases where a tweak breaks native nuance, tone, or constraints.

questions.question: Which document discusses risks of non-native writers creating system prompts?
questions.expected_answer_criteria: The Non-Native Prompt Engineering Risks document.
